delights: It admits when it fails instead of hiding it. Every slot came with a plain-spoken note: "Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance - closest was \"Cacik\" (delivered 78g protein vs a 95g target)." I would rather be told than be fooled.

Nothing on the plate broke a wall. Across all four dishes I saw there was no gluten, soy, nightshade or shellfish - and a dish literally called "Stir-Fried Ground Beef & Broccoli with Rice" came back with no soy sauce in its ingredient list. That is exactly the catch a coeliac needs someone else to make.
The swap genuinely worked and the day re-costed itself. "Classic Salmon & Broccoli with Rice" replaced the yogurt dip and the day moved from 3,136 kcal to 2,988 without me touching anything else.

defects.what: My calorie target points the wrong way. I told it I am going UP from 124.6 kg to 134.4 kg at 2 lb/week and it handed me a number that is a deficit for a 275 lb man training five times a week - it looks like it subtracted 1,000 kcal/day instead of adding it.
The solver failed on all three slots - it never once hit tolerance, it just handed me its least-bad attempt each time.
defects.snippet: Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance - closest was "Chicken with saffron, raisins & pine nuts" (landed 1677 kcal vs a 1249 target).

defects.what: A yogurt-and-cucumber dip was served to me as a 984-kcal dinner, with nothing to eat it with (and I cannot have bread).
defects.snippet: Cacik - Natural Yoghurt: 465 g, Cucumber: 95 g, Lemon Juice: 10 g, Dried Mint: 4 g

defects.what: The dish name lies about what is in it after scaling - sides were cut to 0.5x while the meat doubled, so the dish is 625 g of chicken and a rumour of the recipe it is named after.
defects.snippet: "Chicken with saffron, raisins & pine nuts" - Chicken: 625 g, Pine Nuts: 2 g, Raisins: 6 g, Garlic: 1 g, Thyme: 1 g

defects.what: 555 g of Greek yogurt is called a snack, and the original day put over a kilo of yogurt in front of me across two of three slots (465 g + 555 g).
defects.snippet: snack: "Greek Yogurt, Almonds & Berries" - Greek yogurt, 0%: 555 g

defects.what: I asked for balanced and mediterranean and got a near-keto day: 75 g carbs is 10% of calories and fat is 56%. You cannot fuel five 75-minute weights sessions a week on that, and Mediterranean eating is not fat-only.
defects.snippet: DAY TOTAL: 2988 kcal | P 246 g | F 186 g | C 75 g  (target 2667)

defects.what: Swapping a meal in the obvious way is rejected with an error about something I never sent. PUT .../apply with {"recipeId":"..."} returns 400; it only works if you post the entire alternate object back.
defects.snippet: { "error": "a slot needs at least one ingredient" }

defects.what: Chicken Stock is in my dinner with no gluten-free note. Supermarket stock cubes and cartons routinely carry wheat and soy - as a coeliac this is the one line on the plan I would have to go and verify myself, and the app said nothing.

The mediterranean request is not reflected in how dishes are labelled - a Turkish dip and a Spanish saffron chicken are both filed as western-comfort, and the salmon is filed as american. Only the snack is tagged mediterranean.
defects.snippet: Cacik  cuisine=western-comfort ; Classic Salmon & Broccoli with Rice  [american]

defects.what: Olive oil is labelled as a carbohydrate in two different meals.
Prep time is dishonest for a working day - 34 minutes advertised, but the first instruction needs the yogurt straining overnight.
defects.snippet: prep=34min ... "leave to strain in the fridge for a minimum of 12 hrs"

defects.what: The three alternates offered were really two dishes - the same ground beef and broccoli twice, differing only in which oil it uses.
defects.snippet: 88% Stir-Fried Ground Beef & Broccoli with Rice (Sesame Seed Oil) / 89% Classic Ground Beef & Broccoli with Rice (Olive Oil) / 78% Classic Salmon & Broccoli with Rice

followUp.action: I would not eat 465 g of yogurt dip as my dinner, so I asked for alternates on that slot and swapped one in - the salmon, because it was the only one of the three that read Mediterranean to me.
followUp.endpoint: POST /api/plans/cms6x0nwf0207wlw0c3ima8vh/slots/cms6x0nwh0209wlw0w52djdl1/alternates (200), then PUT .../apply (400, then 200 on retry)
followUp.howItWent: The alternates came back fast and the swap did stick - the plan now reads "Classic Salmon & Broccoli with Rice" and the day re-totalled from 3,136 to 2,988 kcal. But two of the three choices were the same beef-and-broccoli dish with a different oil, all three still carried the same none-fit-within-tolerance warning, and my first apply attempt was rejected 400 with "a slot needs at least one ingredient" until I posted the whole alternate object back.

verdict: It kept me safe - no gluten, soy, nightshade or shellfish anywhere, and it was honest every time it fell short - but it aimed me at a deficit while I am trying to lean bulk, missed tolerance on all three slots, and called a tub of yogurt dinner and half a kilo of yogurt a snack.
